input.question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?
input.ground_truth: F-35 is pretty much 3 different planes, that look similar. * Navy version has different wings and modifications to frame to support carrier landing. * Marine version has VSTOL. * Air Force version has better performance.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friend both want to build a really cool toy car. You want yours to do lots of different things—fly like a plane, drive on the ground, and even hide from radar. Your friend just wants his to fly really fast and look cool.

Now, you decide your toy car needs to be able to play with all your other toys (work with other machines), fit in different garages (be used by many countries), and change its shape a little bit (different versions for different jobs). So, you have to make lots and lots of changes and try many different ideas to make sure it works just right for everyone.

Your friend’s toy car was also supposed to do some cool things, but not as many different things as yours. But by the time he finished, he already spent a lot of time and money making sure his car was super safe and perfect, because it was the first really special toy car like that.

But you kept changing your toy car’s plan to make it do even more things, and every time you changed something, it cost more money and took more time. Also, lots of grown-ups had to check and double-check everything to make sure your toy car was safe and could do all the jobs you wanted.

So, even though your toy car (the F-35) wasn’t supposed to be as fancy as your friend’s (the F-22), you wanted it to do so many different things for so many people that it ended up costing way more to make!
